name: Sredno Vodno – Millennium Cross
shortDescription: The standard out-and-back climb from Sredno Vodno to the Millennium Cross on Krstovar.
description: This popular Skopje route starts at the Sredno Vodno cable-car station and climbs on signed forest paths toward Krstovar (1,066 m), the summit crowned by the Millennium Cross. The upper slopes open to broad views across Skopje and the surrounding mountains. Several path variants exist, so the recorded distance represents the main round trip.

name: Matka Canyon – St. Nicholas Šiševski Monastery
shortDescription: A short, steep canyon hike from Matka to St. Nicholas Šiševski Monastery.
description: From the bridge and kayaking area at Matka, the footpath climbs above the Treska reservoir to the medieval St. Nicholas Šiševski Monastery on Vodno's western slope. The monastery stands roughly 160 metres above the lake and is inaccessible by road. The path is rocky and can be slippery after rain; this is a different outing from the mostly level path that follows the reservoir shoreline.

images.caption: Matka Canyon and the Treska reservoir

name: Ljuboten Mountain Hut – Ljuboten Peak
shortDescription: A demanding ascent from the historic Ljuboten hut to the mountain's distinctive border summit.
description: From Mountain Hut Ljuboten above Staro Selo, the route leaves the forest belt and climbs through pasture toward the prominent pyramidal summit of Ljuboten (2,498 m). The upper section is exposed and the summit lies on the Kosovo border, so hikers should carry offline navigation and check current border guidance. The hut is also the northern gateway of the High Scardus Trail.

name: Popova Šapka – Titov Vrv
shortDescription: The classic long route from Popova Šapka to Titov Vrv, the highest summit of Šar Mountain.
description: The marked route begins at Popova Šapka and crosses open high-mountain terrain via the Ceripašina and Bakardan area before the final climb to Titov Vrv (2,747 m). A stone tower marks the summit, with views toward the Pena headwaters and Šar Mountain's glacial lakes. The route is long, exposed and vulnerable to rapid weather changes; reliable navigation and strong fitness are essential.

name: Strezimir – Golem Korab
shortDescription: The standard ascent from Strezimir to Golem Korab, the highest point in North Macedonia.
description: This remote route starts at Strezimir (about 1,420 m) in the upper Radika valley and climbs broad pasture, mountain streams and rocky upper slopes to Golem Korab (2,764 m), the highest point of North Macedonia and Albania. The summit follows the international border, access roads can be rough, and cloud makes navigation difficult. Hikers should check current access requirements before departure and carry sufficient water and offline mapping.

name: Galičica Pass – Magaro Peak
shortDescription: The national park's classic climb from Galičica Pass to Magaro Peak.
description: Starting beside regional road P-504 at Galičica Pass, this signed circuit climbs through limestone grassland to Magaro (2,255 m), the highest summit in the national park. In clear weather the ridge gives simultaneous views of Lake Ohrid and Lake Prespa. The terrain is exposed with little shade or water, and summer hikers should start early.

name: Pelister Info Center – Pelister Peak via Bolnici
shortDescription: The official one-way ascent from the Pelister Info Center to Pelister Peak via Bolnici.
description: The park's official Bolnici route begins at the Information Center at 7 Kladenci, passes Hotel Molika and Kopanki, then crosses the distinctive stone field known as Bolnici before reaching Pelister Peak (2,601 m). It moves from molika pine forest into exposed alpine terrain and opens views over Pelagonia, Prespa and the Baba massif. The published 11 km and 4.5–5 hour figures are one way; plan additional time and distance for the return.

name: Adžibarica – Zelen Breg
shortDescription: The customary round trip from Adžibarica above Smrdliva Voda to Kožuf's highest summit.
description: The route begins in the Adžibarica area above Smrdliva Voda and climbs toward Zelen Breg (about 2,170 m), the rounded highest summit of Kožuf. Forest and high pasture give way to wide southern views toward the sharper Kožuf ridges and the Thessaloniki plain. The tourism authority estimates about six hours for the return hike; the area is remote and hikers should carry navigation and water.

name: Mountain Hut Čeples – Solunska Glava
shortDescription: The summer route from Mountain Hut Čeples to Solunska Glava and back.
description: From Mountain Hut Čeples (about 1,410 m), the marked summer route climbs through beech forest toward Dolna and Gorna Babina Dupka, then crosses exposed high ground to Solunska Glava (2,540 m). The summit overlooks Pelagonia and the connected Jakupica, Dautica and Karadžica massifs. Published guidance gives roughly 7.5 km and four hours to the summit, plus about three hours for the return; avoid the winter line unless properly equipped and experienced.

name: Popova Šapka – Gorna Lešnica – Lešnica
shortDescription: A marked traverse from Popova Šapka through Gorna Lešnica to the Lešnica valley.
description: Beginning at the information board in central Popova Šapka, the marked trail passes above the Jelak hut, crosses pasture near Ceripašinsko Bačilo and Plat, then descends through Gorna Lešnica into the canyon and valley of Lešnica. The route combines open views of Šar Mountain's central peaks with forest, streams and the Gorna Lešnica waterfall. Water is usually available along the route, but the return climb from the valley must be included in planning.

name: Nikiforovo – Sandaktaš Peak
shortDescription: A marked Bistra Mountain ascent from Nikiforovo to Sandaktaš Peak.
description: The route starts in Nikiforovo beside Mavrovo Lake, follows the Petilepska River through forest to the Petti Leb spring, then continues across open pasture to Sandaktaš (about 1,980 m). It is an established Mavrovo National Park trail tied to local St. Panteleimon traditions. The upper pasture is exposed and requires careful sign-following in fog; fill water at the village or Petti Leb.

name: Prilep – Treskavec Monastery
shortDescription: The marked one-way climb from Prilep's northern edge to Treskavec Monastery.
description: The trail climbs from above Prilep through the granite landscape below Markovi Kuli and Zlatovrv to the 12th-century Treskavec Monastery. It offers extensive views over the Pelagonia plain and passes striking boulders and exposed slabs. The published 6.7 km figure is one way; a short fixed rope assists one steeper rock section, and smooth granite becomes hazardous in rain or snow.

name: Kruševo – Mečkin Kamen
shortDescription: A highland walk from Kruševo to the Mečkin Kamen memorial site.
description: The route leaves the high town of Kruševo and follows forest roads and open upland terrain toward Mečkin Kamen, the memorial landscape associated with Pitu Guli and the Ilinden Uprising of 1903. The walking is technically straightforward and can be combined with visits to Kruševo's other monuments. Snow and ice are common in winter because the route remains near 1,200–1,400 metres.

name: Kokino – Tatićev Kamen
shortDescription: A short rocky approach from the road end below Tatićev Kamen to the Bronze Age site.
description: The route climbs the volcanic hill of Tatićev Kamen above Kokino to a Bronze Age archaeological complex at roughly 1,010–1,030 metres. Two rock platforms preserve carved markers and stone seats associated with observations of the sun and moon. This is a compact archaeological walk rather than a full mountain day; the final rock is uneven and exposed.

name: Ramne – Letnica – Visok Vrv – Krstec – Velestovo
shortDescription: A Galičica National Park traverse between Ramne and Velestovo above Ohrid.
description: This park-listed point-to-point route links Ramne with Velestovo via Letnica, Visok Vrv and Krstec on Galičica's western slopes. It alternates woodland and open high ground, with repeated views over Ohrid and Lake Ohrid. Arrange return transport between the villages, carry water, and confirm current marking and conditions with the national park information center before setting out.

name: Smolari – Smolare Waterfall
shortDescription: The maintained footpath from the Smolari trailhead to Smolare Waterfall on Belasica.
description: A 580-metre pedestrian path follows the Lomnica River through old beech forest to Smolare Waterfall, returning by the same route. Around 300 local-stone steps, a wooden bridge and a gazebo make the waterfall accessible, but the steps can be wet and slippery. The permanent waterfall drops about 39.5 metres and is the highest in North Macedonia.

name: Berovo Lake – Dvorište – Bela Voda
shortDescription: A point-to-point route from Berovo Lake through Dvorište to Bela Voda.
description: This substantial Maleševo route begins where the Klepalo River enters Berovo Lake, climbs through pine and beech forest past Bačilo Kalamadevski, and reaches Babin Čukar (1,403 m). It continues by the Turtela archaeological site and St. Ilija church, through Dvorište, and finishes at Bela Voda on Ogražden. The 20 km route is point-to-point, so return transport should be arranged in advance.

name: Nežilovo – Mountain Hut Čeples
shortDescription: The direct one-way forest ascent from Nežilovo to Mountain Hut Čeples.
description: The direct hiking path begins near the fish restaurant in Nežilovo and climbs about 700 metres through forest to Mountain Hut Čeples, the principal base for Solunska Glava and the Babuna headwaters. Published guidance gives 5 km and about 2.5 hours one way. A separate 11 km dirt-road option visits the Babuna springs; do not confuse its longer distance with this direct footpath.

name: Demir Kapija – Prosek Fortress and Prozori Caves
shortDescription: A steep historical hike from Demir Kapija to the ruins of Prosek Fortress.
description: The route climbs the limestone side of the Demir Kapija gorge to the remains of Prosek, a fortified settlement occupying a strategic plateau above a bend of the Vardar. The ascent combines canyon views, dry Mediterranean vegetation and archaeological remains from several periods. It is a physically demanding, exposed route with little shade; avoid the hottest part of summer days and stay back from cliff edges. The marked path continues past the fortress rocks to the Prozori (Windows) caves high above the gorge, where the recorded route turns back.

name: Gradec – Lisec Peak
shortDescription: The northern approach from Gradec to Lisec, the highest summit of Plačkovica.
description: The easiest established approach to Lisec (1,754 m) starts from the northern side near Gradec and climbs forest roads and ridge terrain for about 16 km to the summit. Lisec is the highest point of Plačkovica and commands wide views across eastern North Macedonia. The stated distance is one way; route marking varies, so offline navigation is recommended.
